patients.label: Case 1

identity_evidence.quote: Case 1 involved a 50-year-old man diagnosed with chronic ITP.

attribution_limitations: Case 1 relapse timing and duration of response are reported inconsistently: relapse after 6 months (discussion), PLT 31 at 20 days after hetrombopag discontinuation with DoR 23 months (results), DoR 23+ months (Table 1), and the abstract places the fall to 31 after 6 months of DoR.
The abstract DoR range 3 to 27 months does not match the Table 1 DoR values (23+, 27+, 29+, 12).
Rituximab for Case 1 is consistent across table and text; figure 1 prints a total rituximab dose of 800 mg that the text does not state.

Figure 1 prints "PLT <1" at the point where the text gives a platelet count below 10 after eltrombopag discontinuation, prints "PLT 2" after the hetrombopag and danazol label, and shows an RTX 800mg first dose; these figure-only values are compatible with or absent from the text and are kept in the visual record only.

patients.label: Case 2

identity_evidence.quote: Case 2 involved a 55-year-old woman diagnosed with acute ITP.

attribution_limitations: The Discussion says case 2 relapsed after combination therapy, but the Results describe no medication, platelets maintained at 260-270 and DoR >27 months (Table 1 27+). The abstract says the two patients other than the first and third remained in sustained CR.

Anti-CD20 agent for case 2: Table 1 lists RTX and the Results name rituximab (Discussion: two patients received each agent), but the Methods say the other patients received ripertamab and figure 1 prints ripertamab for case 2. Unlike cases 3 and 4, two structured statements disagree here (Table 1 RTX versus the Methods sentence, with Figure 1 printing RPT doses). The Results opener "rituximab-hetrombopag therapy" is weak evidence because the same wording also opens the case 3 and case 4 paragraphs, where Table 1, the Methods, Figure 1 and the next sentences name ripertamab; there the agent is recorded as ripertamab with an ambiguity, here it stays unresolved.
Platelet counts in Table 1 (After the treatment 655, Highest 833) differ from the Results values (258 at CR, 393 after second dose, 260-270 maintained).

patients.label: Case 3

identity_evidence.quote: Case 3 involved a 49-year-old woman diagnosed with chronic ITP.

attribution_limitations: The Results say rituximab-hetrombopag therapy for 9 days, but Table 1, the Methods and later Results text name ripertamab for case 3; Figure 1 shows a ripertamab course and a later rituximab course.
Case 3 is typed chronic ITP in Table 1 and the narrative, while the abstract and Discussion call it secondary ITP due to Sjögren syndrome.
The start point of "After 4 months" is not stated in its sentence.

patients.label: Case 4

identity_evidence.quote: Case 4 involved a 58-year-old man diagnosed with acute ITP.

attribution_limitations: The Results say rituximab-hetrombopag therapy for 2 days, but Table 1, the Methods and the next Results sentence name ripertamab for case 4.
Platelet count before the treatment is 28 in Table 1 but 29 at the preceding point in the narrative (after hetrombopag dose increase).
Table 1 lists DoR 12 (no plus sign) while the Results state >12 months.
